we have demonstrated the possibility to compensate the effects of the different electron rise time of the pixels in a CZT/CdZTe detector using a biparametric shaping amplifier.

the twin shaping technique can improve the energy resolution of CZT/CdZnTe detectors, but the improvement is not significant enough to justify the use of such a complex technique in a real application.

In summary, our research is concerned with

- the development of a readout electronics based on a biparametric technique for compensating the charge signals in CdZnTe detectors, - the development of an algorithm for the automatic correction of the charge signals in a large number of pixels, - the study of the distribution of the compensation parameters, - the comparison between the biparametric approach and other techniques, - the development and the test of a readout integrated electronics for multipixel detectors.
the development and testing of a novel readout electronics for CZT detectors, with the goal to provide a high performance, compact and low cost solution for space and ground based applications.
the development of new technologies and methods for improving the performance of the detectors for space applications.

the use of the biparametrical method is a very powerful and promising tool for compensating the charge collection non uniformity in CdTe/CdZnTe detectors.
